simple.meaning: טָרִי (ṭârîy) is a Hebrew word meaning “properly, dripping ; hence, fresh (i.e. recently made such).” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: טָרִי (H2961) appears 2 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Judges 15:15, with occurrences in Judges, Isaiah.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to טָרִי (H2961) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in טָרִי (H2961) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: טָרִי (ṭârîy) / H2961 is traced through Judges 15:15, Isaiah 1:6 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.short: properly, dripping ; hence, fresh (i.e. recently made such)
definitions.full: H2961. tari [ טָרִי ] adjective fresh , only feminine singular טְרִיָּה fresh , טְרִיָּה לְחִיחֲֿמוֺר Judg 15:15 the fresh jawbone of an ass , i.e. not yet dry and brittle; ט ׳מַכָּה Isa 1:6 fresh, raw wound , not yield healed or even treated (so Ges Ew Brd Di Du; festering De Che).
definitions.rootNote: from an unused root apparently meaning to be moist ;

occurrences.englishText: He found a fresh jawbone of a donkey, put out his hand, took it, and struck a thousand men with it.
